messages:
Maria: Heads up — planning to cut the release branch for v2.0 tomorrow at 10:00 PT. This is a major bump due to the serialization format change. Need someone to create the branch and we should lock down backport rules and the cherry-pick queue today. Quick answers please.

Jon: A couple quick Qs — cutoff for docs-only and dependency bumps? Also who will own the actual branch create?

Maria: Docs-only can be backported if it's strictly doc text and no code changes. Dependency bumps: prefer to land on main and backport rarely (security fixes ok). Looking for someone to create the release/* branch — willing to volunteer? @jon ? :pray:

Jon: I can create the branch. Will do at the scheduled time unless someone needs earlier. Command I'll run is:
```
git checkout -b release/v2.0 main
git push origin release/v2.0
```
Open to changes if infra wants a different base.

Sophia: Important: the serialization change touches the migration path. That one must stay on main and cannot be backported. Any PR that touches schema/migrations -> no backport.

Kevin: For the cherry-pick flow, can we standardize on this pattern?
1) add label backport/candidate
2) ping @kevin in the PR
3) once accepted, I or the release lead will cherry-pick with `git cherry-pick -x` and open PR against release/v2.0
Also please add a short justification in the PR body (risk, test plan).

Maria: +1 to Kevin's flow. Let's also require the label `backport/approved` before we merge into release branch. Keeps things gated.

Alex: Changelog nudge: please add a short blurb to the PR with `changelog: user-facing summary` and add the `changelog-needed` label. We'll aggregate into the release notes.

Jon: Noted. Also reminder to bump the package version in the usual places. Example:
```
# python package
- bump version in setup.cfg and pyproject.toml
# npm package
- bump package.json
```
I'll include a checklist when I open the branch.

Kevin: I'll stand up a small backport queue tonight. Please add PRs to the backport board column named "v2.0 candidates" (I'll update the board). I'll triage for risk and conflict.

Sophia: QA: I'll take point on smoke tests for release/v2.0. If a cherry-pick changes serialization bits, I will block. Please @mention me on those PRs.

Maria: Ownership summary: Jon = create branch + initial push, Kevin = cherry-pick triage, Sophia = QA on release branch, Alex = changelog aggregator, Maria = final signoff. Everyone ok? :white_check_mark:

Kevin: ok from me.

Alex: ok. I'll create a tiny template for changelog lines and post it to #eng-releases so folks can copy.

Jon: created the branch early (requested a pre-cut). Branch is up: release/v2.0 -> sha abcdef1. PR protection rules are being applied. Link: https://git.example.com/redwood/repo/branch/release/v2.0

release-bot: Branch created: release/v2.0 by Jon at abcdef1 — protection rules: required-reviews=2, status-checks=ci, no-force-push.

devops-bot: FYI deployed mirror for release testing in staging cluster: staging-v2.0 (tags: release/v2.0). Run smoke suite with `./scripts/smoke.sh --env staging-v2.0`

Maria: Amazing — thanks Jon and team. Next steps:
- Kevin: start triage of backport candidates (please tag high-risk)
- Alex: post changelog template and collect entries
- Sophia: run smoke on staging after each cherry-pick merge
- Jon: keep branch protection on, and ping me for final cut.

If anything blocks we escalate to oncall. Otherwise I'll post a final reminder at 09:30 PT tomorrow.

Kevin: I'll post an initial queue in ~30m.

Sophia: I'll kick off the first smoke run now.

Maria: Thanks all. :rocket:
